questions.question: Which manager guided West Ham United to a 7th-place Premier League finish and the FA Cup final in the 2005–06 season, securing European qualification in their first year back in the top flight?
questions.explanation: Alan Pardew won promotion with West Ham in 2005 and immediately led them to a 7th-place finish and an unforgettable 3–3 FA Cup final against Liverpool.
questions.anchorClues: Alan Pardew / West Ham United 2005–06 season

questions.question: True or False: Sunderland's Stadium of Light hosted the senior England national team for a competitive UEFA European Championship qualifier in April 2003.
questions.explanation: England played Turkey at the Stadium of Light in a Euro 2004 qualifier on 2 April 2003, securing a 2–0 victory thanks to goals from Darius Vassell and David Beckham.
questions.anchorClues: Stadium of Light / England vs Turkey Euro 2004 qualifier

questions.question: Which club became the first team to defeat Pep Guardiola's Manchester City in the Premier League during their 'Centurions' 2017–18 campaign, ending City's 22-match unbeaten league run in January 2018?
questions.explanation: Jürgen Klopp's Liverpool earned a thrilling 4–3 victory at Anfield in January 2018, handing Manchester City their first league defeat of the season.

questions.question: Which historic ground served as Derby County's home stadium for 102 years before the club relocated to Pride Park Stadium in 1997?
questions.explanation: Derby County played at the famous Baseball Ground from 1895 until May 1997, hosting their first Premier League campaign there in 1996–97.
questions.anchorClues: Baseball Ground / Derby County home stadium

questions.question: True or False: Chelsea went through their entire 2004–05 title-winning Premier League campaign without suffering a single defeat at Stamford Bridge.
questions.explanation: José Mourinho turned Stamford Bridge into a fortress in 2004–05, with Chelsea recording 14 wins and 5 draws at home while conceding just six league goals in SW6.
questions.anchorClues: Chelsea unbeaten home record Stamford Bridge 2004–05

questions.question: Which club spent 128 days at the top of the Premier League table during the 2013–14 campaign—the most of any team that season—before eventually finishing in 4th place?
questions.explanation: Arsène Wenger's Arsenal led the table for a total of 128 days between September 2013 and February 2014 before late-season stumbles saw Manchester City claim the title.
questions.anchorClues: Arsenal 128 days top of Premier League table 2013–14

questions.question: Which squad number was assigned to French midfielder N'Golo Kanté throughout his trophy-laden seven seasons at Chelsea, winning the Premier League, Champions League, and FA Cup?
questions.explanation: N'Golo Kanté wore the number 7 shirt for Chelsea between 2016 and 2023, making 269 appearances across all competitions.

questions.question: Which club brought an end to Chelsea's record 86-game unbeaten home league run at Stamford Bridge with a 1–0 victory in October 2008?
questions.explanation: A deflected strike from Xabi Alonso earned Rafa Benítez's Liverpool a 1–0 victory at Stamford Bridge, ending Chelsea's four-year, 86-match unbeaten home streak.
questions.anchorClues: Liverpool end Chelsea 86 home unbeaten run 2008

questions.question: Which manager took charge of Southampton in January 2013 and guided them to an 8th-place Premier League finish with 56 points in his only full season at the club?
questions.explanation: Mauricio Pochettino transformed Southampton's playing style during the 2013–14 season before being appointed Tottenham Hotspur manager in May 2014.

questions.question: Which Dutch forward holds the Premier League record for scoring in the most consecutive away matches, finding the net in nine straight away appearances during the 2010–11 season?
questions.explanation: Robin van Persie scored in nine consecutive Premier League away fixtures for Arsenal between January and May 2011, establishing a top-flight record.
questions.anchorClues: Robin van Persie 9 consecutive away goals record 2010–11
